provenance.note: Hyperparameters pinned verbatim from the official Alpha158 benchmark workflows. No tuning. MASTER not included: no Qlib-contrib implementation exists at v0.9.6 or main (checked 2026-10-18).

data_convention.features: clean CSI300 panel (Alpha158 columns) as consumed by every arm. Per-model feature sets follow the official v0.9.6 yamls: LSTM/GRU/ALSTM/Transformer configs specify FilterCol col_list (20 columns, verbatim below); XGBoost and DoubleEnsemble configs specify NO FilterCol and therefore use the full 158-column Alpha158 handler. No extra infer processors (the clean panel is already the W1-verified processed input: RobustZScoreNorm fit 2008-01-01..train_end, fillna(0)).
data_convention.label: z_r1 (clean 1-day label, close(t+2)/close(t+1)-1, cross-sectionally z-scored; same definition as the ridge/LightGBM r1 cells of Section 8A). Qlib's own CSRankNorm label processor (explicit in the NN yamls, class-default for XGB/DE) is NOT re-applied; this is the only deviation from the published pipelines.
data_convention.seed_policy: LSTM/GRU/ALSTM: seeds 1-3 (stochastic, no config seed; global torch/np seeding). DoubleEnsemble: seeds 1-3 (np-seeded sample reweighting; no config seed). XGBoost: single run at xgboost's default seed 0 (deterministic single-machine hist). Transformer: single run at its config seed 0 (deterministic by configuration).

Transformer.note: all other hyperparameters = class defaults of qlib v0.9.6 pytorch_transformer_ts.TransformerModel

reported_edge_caution: Qlib's published benchmark numbers use train 2008-2014 / valid 2015-2016 / test 2017-2020-08 and the qlib data handler; any comparison to published IC/excess must state the different windows and pipeline (this study: clean panel, train 2008-2018, valid 2019-2020, rule selection 2021-2022).
